headline: Chilly, possibly frosty mornings early in the week; quiet, with light rain possible late week.
summary: A pocket of cold air high in the atmosphere is sliding south offshore, so western Washington stays mostly quiet. Cool mornings are the main story: Monday lows are in the mid 30s around Olympia and south along I-5, and in the mid 40s elsewhere. Tuesday mornings are colder, so frost is possible in the south Sound, Chehalis Valley, the Cascades, and valleys, with patchy fog in typical spots early in the week. Later in the week, a weak system may bring light rain Thursday into Friday. If it does, snow could fall to about 4,000 to 4,500 feet, with a few flurries there and higher. Forecasters expect little impact but are less sure where the system will be by Friday into the weekend.
